When an egg (oocyte) is released from the ovary during ovulation, the follicle that contained the egg remains behind. This ruptured follicle undergoes a transformation and becomes the corpus luteum, which is a temporary endocrine structure that secretes progesterone and some estrogen to prepare the uterine lining for potential implantation.
